content.value: Artificial crafting uses one Artificial Tome at the [[article/runic_altar|Runic Altar]], followed by a saved choice at the [[article/artificial_tome|Artificial Runic Altar]]. It works on Rare, non-Unique equipment.

Choose Add to free slot, or select an editable rune to replace. A full item requires a selected replacement; no existing rune is removed randomly.
A replacement spends the tome and presents a comparison. Choose Use new to accept the artificial marker, or Keep current to retain your equipment. Resolve this comparison before using the [[article/artificial_tome|Artificial Runic Altar]].
The marker reserves an eligible prefix or suffix slot. Only one artificial marker or revealed artificial rune may remain on an item.

Insert the marked item into the [[article/artificial_tome|Artificial Runic Altar]]. No second tome is needed.
The altar saves up to three compatible, nonduplicate rune families with exact tiers and numeric values. Families use the same weight rules as random crafting.
Options use the equipment's best three eligible tiers, or fewer when only one or two tiers are allowed. A shield or bow always receives T10. A diamond base can offer T8-T10; never T1-T7.
Select a card, inspect its preview, and confirm Reveal rune. The other saved choices disappear.

Options are stored on the equipment. Removing it, closing the screen or restarting does not reroll them. Protected rune properties remain untouched. Revealed artificial runes can later be selected for ordinary Divine, Chaos or Annulment crafting.
